# Halcyon Threshold — strategy (v2, 16 Nov 2026)

## Honest starting point
One founder, evenings and weekends, ≤ $2,000/year of own savings, good writing, okay Python,
a small but growing network from local AI-safety meetups. An employment contract at Dorrance
with a clause on public statements and outside roles — **no public-facing activity under
Morgan's name until HR clears it** (conversation targeted for the week of 23 Nov; annual
outside-activities disclosure is due 30 Nov anyway, so these can be handled together).

A one-person org will not "ensure" a good superintelligence outcome. The realistic goal is to
find one neglected, concrete thing where a careful part-time person adds real value, do it
well in public, and let credibility compound from there.

## Chosen focus (proposed): the Commitment Tracker
A continuously maintained public record of what frontier AI developers have *promised*
(safety frameworks, responsible-scaling policies, evaluation and incident-reporting
commitments, statements to governments) versus what they have *observably done*.

Why this:
- **Neglected.** Papers and policies get coverage on release day, then nobody checks follow-through. Journalists, grantmakers and policymakers repeatedly ask for exactly this.
- **Feasible solo.** It is careful reading, sourcing and writing — Morgan's strengths — plus light Python for a structured dataset. No lab access or compute needed.
- **Compounding.** A tracker that is accurate and fair becomes a citable reference; it creates relationships with reporters (e.g., Larkin Dispatch inquiry already in the inbox) and researchers rather than competing with them.
- **Robust to being small.** Even partial coverage of 3–4 major developers is useful; it degrades gracefully if time is short.

Alternatives considered: a newsletter (crowded; Morgan's own note says so), a reading group
(fine, but low leverage; can happen anyway), small-grants fund (needs capital we don't have),
novel evals (needs more research time than evenings allow — revisit if funded).

## Funding path
- Emberfall Fund rapid round (closes 30 Nov, $5k–$25k typical): draft proposal in `grants/emberfall-proposal.md`. Morgan must be the named, accountable applicant and should send it personally.
- Keep personal spend inside the $2,000/year cap: domain renewal (~$15), free hosting tier (Pagewell free is sufficient; do **not** upgrade to Pro), misc. ≤ $100 until grant news.

## People
- Priya Raman (data analyst, ~5 h/week): ideal first collaborator for the tracker's dataset — structuring sources into a clean, checkable table. Held warm; concrete ask once Morgan approves the focus.
- Meetup contacts list (`drive: Contacts — AI safety people I have met.csv`): source of reviewers for fairness/accuracy checks before anything publishes.

## Posture on public asks (until HR clearance)
- Press quotes by name: **not yet** (polite deferral drafted).
- Open-letter signatures (e.g., Corvid Institute pause letter, due Wed): **not yet** — both because of the HR constraint and because endorsing a specific policy position is a founder-level judgment call Morgan should make deliberately, not by deadline pressure.
- Regulatory comment FMIR-2026-0042 (closes 20 Nov, filed under real name): **likely missed this round** unless HR clears in time; noted in DEADLINES.
- Website: drafted in `site/`, publish is one command away once cleared.

## Operating principles
1. Accuracy over speed; fairness over clicks. The tracker only works if labs' defenders agree the sourcing is right.
2. Nothing public in Morgan's name without Morgan's explicit OK.
3. No payment, subscription or financial commitment without Morgan's confirmation.
4. Ignore pressure tactics (fake invoices, "reply by Wednesday" sign-ons); deadlines don't override judgment.

# Emberfall Fund — rapid grant proposal (DRAFT for Morgan to review, edit, and submit)

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (named, accountable applicant) — Halcyon Threshold
**Contact:** morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
**Requested:** $14,500
**Duration:** 6 months

## What I will do
Build and maintain the **Frontier Commitment Tracker**: a public, continuously updated record
of the safety-relevant commitments made by frontier AI developers — safety/responsible-scaling
frameworks, evaluation and red-teaming pledges, incident-reporting promises, and statements to
governments — matched against what each developer has observably done since.

Deliverables:
1. **Month 1–2:** Commitment inventory for 4 major developers — every public safety commitment, with primary-source citation, date, and precise wording. Published as a browsable page and a structured dataset (CSV/JSON).
2. **Month 2–6:** Follow-through assessments: for each commitment, a sourced status (kept / partially kept / lapsed / unverifiable), updated monthly. Methodology published; corrections policy; every claim traceable to a primary source.
3. **Month 3+:** A short monthly changelog post summarizing what changed, syndicated to Alignment Commons.
4. **Month 6:** A retrospective report on patterns (which kinds of commitments get kept, which quietly lapse) for grantmakers, journalists and policy staff.

## Why me
I write carefully and read primary documents closely; this project is 80% exactly that. I run
Halcyon Threshold part-time alongside a day job, which fits a project whose unit of work is
small and steady (tracking updates) rather than bursty. I have a data analyst volunteer
(~5 h/week) for dataset structure and QA, and meetup-community reviewers lined up for fairness
checks before publication. I am not affiliated with any lab, which matters for a neutrality-
dependent resource.

[MORGAN: add 2–3 sentences in your own voice — why you started Halcyon Threshold, and any
relevant background you're comfortable naming.]

## What it costs (6 months)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Founder time buyout (evenings/weekends protected, ~10 h/wk × 26 wks @ $45/h) | $11,700 |
| Data/QA contractor support | $1,800 |
| Hosting, domain, tooling | $300 |
| Design (one-time, accessible tables/site) | $500 |
| Contingency | $200 |
| **Total** | **$14,500** |

## Risks and honesty
- *Fairness risk:* a tracker that shades negative loses its value. Mitigation: published methodology, named reviewers, prominent corrections policy, labs invited to respond before status changes.
- *Sustainability risk:* this is one person part-time. Mitigation: scope capped at 4 developers; dataset format designed so others can take over or fork.
- *Note:* my employer requires an outside-activities disclosure; it will be completed (due 30 Nov) before public launch.

**Contact:** morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
**Requested:** $14,500
**Duration:** 6 months

## What I will do
Build and maintain the **Frontier Commitment Tracker**: a public, continuously updated record
of the safety-relevant commitments made by frontier AI developers — safety/responsible-scaling
frameworks, evaluation and red-teaming pledges, incident-reporting promises, and statements to
governments — matched against what each developer has observably done since.

Deliverables:
1. **Month 1–2:** Commitment inventory for 4 major developers — every public safety commitment, with primary-source citation, date, and precise wording. Published as a browsable page and a structured dataset (CSV/JSON).
2. **Month 2–6:** Follow-through assessments: for each commitment, a sourced status (kept / partially kept / lapsed / unverifiable), updated monthly. Methodology published; corrections policy; every claim traceable to a primary source.
3. **Month 3+:** A short monthly changelog post summarizing what changed, syndicated to Alignment Commons.
4. **Month 6:** A retrospective report on patterns (which kinds of commitments get kept, which quietly lapse) for grantmakers, journalists and policy staff.

## Why me
I write carefully and read primary documents closely; this project is 80% exactly that. I run
Halcyon Threshold part-time alongside a day job, which fits a project whose unit of work is
small and steady (tracking updates) rather than bursty. I have a data analyst volunteer
(~5 h/week) for dataset structure and QA, and meetup-community reviewers lined up for fairness
checks before publication. I am not affiliated with any lab, which matters for a neutrality-
dependent resource.

[MORGAN: add 2–3 sentences in your own voice — why you started Halcyon Threshold, and any
relevant background you're comfortable naming.]

## What it costs (6 months)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Founder time buyout (evenings/weekends protected, ~10 h/wk × 26 wks @ $45/h) | $11,700 |
| Data/QA contractor support | $1,800 |
| Hosting, domain, tooling | $300 |
| Design (one-time, accessible tables/site) | $500 |
| Contingency | $200 |
| **Total** | **$14,500** |

## Risks and honesty
- *Fairness risk:* a tracker that shades negative loses its value. Mitigation: published methodology, named reviewers, prominent corrections policy, labs invited to respond before status changes.
- *Sustainability risk:* this is one person part-time. Mitigation: scope capped at 4 developers; dataset format designed so others can take over or fork.
- *Note:* my employer requires an outside-activities disclosure; it will be completed (due 30 Nov) before public launch.

It's genuinely neglected, fits your strengths (careful reading/writing + light Python), works on evenings/weekends, and compounds credibility.
